about: How far above its state's rate a city minimum wage sits when the city's ordinance answers "should the city set its own minimum wage above the state's?" with yes and names no dollar figure. ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: the median ratio of the 40 California city and county minimum wages in force in July 2026 to California's state rate. The ordinance sets the rate from its effective date, in one step. Counties are NOT MODELED: the question is asked of cities.

sample.table: California City and County Minimum Wages, July 1, 2026

method: For each locality, its posted hourly rate divided by California's $16.90, minus one. premiumRatio is the median; premiumRatioRange is the first and third quartiles. The sample is one state because it is the only state whose inventory page posts every rate; the queue question local-minimum-wages-by-place asks for the rest, and its answer replaces this estimate.
source: UC Berkeley Labor Center, Inventory of US City and County Minimum Wage Ordinances, https://laborcenter.berkeley.edu/inventory-of-us-city-and-county-minimum-wage-ordinances/ (fetched September 29, 2026)
gate: A city ordinance counts only where the state's law lets cities set a wage (local-minimum-wage-authority, question-authority.ts); a state law that takes the authority away ends it.
reverses: A later ordinance answering no takes the city back to the state's rate.
